design.why_ResidualInRegion: NotProven::ResidualInRegion is documented as the independent checks of the saved bytes (flatten::check_flattened, flatten_purge::check_document) finding a mismatch; the new rule is such a check on the saved bytes. PaintedSourceKept is painted-source specific, RegionIncomplete is selector specific. No new variant was needed
design.why_saved_file: the check reads the SAVED document (like the /Pg scan), so it sees exactly what a viewer gets and cannot disagree with the writer
design.rule: lead decision: any element the purge cannot place on a kept page counts (no /Pg, or a /Pg not resolvable to a kept page). Over-reporting accepted: a Document element without /Pg of a direct-root tree counts
design.no_edit: the tree is not edited (lead: fail closed only); the text stays in the file and is reported
design.why_unread_only: lead scope: the new clause reads only what neutralize_structure could not (elements below a /K array reached through a reference or nested in a /K array), so an edited tree read through direct arrays reports exactly what it reported before (control F; the existing tests structure_and_widgets_of_flattened_pages_are_removed and flattened_page_annotations_leave_and_structure_elements_stay stay flattened)
design.page_rule: same as the direct-root rule: own /Pg, else the nearest ancestor element's, must name a kept page of the saved file; the check reads the SAVED file, where a parent neutralized for a flattened /Pg has lost it, so its child below an indirect array has no page and counts (probe A)
design.why_nested_arrays: an array inside a /K array is not read by the purge either (not a conforming spelling, but the same silent skip); the walk used to ignore any /K item that resolves to an array, so it now descends with unread set (tests: cases "an array reference listed inside a direct /K array" and "an array written inside a direct /K array"; mutant m3)
design.why_k_only: in an edited tree only the root /K is walked (not /ParentTree, /IDTree): a conforming tree lists every element under /K, the parent tree walk would add steps and false positives on large legitimate documents; elements only reachable from the parent tree or id tree of an edited tree are therefore not read (residual below)

residuals: Over-reporting (accepted by the lead decision): in a direct or chain-reached tree every element without a kept /Pg on its path counts, text-bearing or not

Over-reporting in an edited tree (same stance, new in 54c60f9): an element below a /K array that is a reference, with no kept page on its path and a STRUCT_TEXT_KEYS key (a Document, Sect or Table element with /Lang, /A, /C, /ID or /T and no /Pg, whose children carry kept /Pg), counts; so a file whose structure tree uses indirect /K arrays and has such elements reads region_flattened false after a page is flattened. Not probed on a real corpus file. PLR-097 option 1 would remove the text of the elements it can place instead of reporting

The bounds count one more in an edited tree too: an edited tree deeper than Limits::max_depth (32) levels or with more than Limits::max_objects (200000) /K items now reads region_flattened false (before: not read). A legitimate document that deep or that large is over-reported; the bound itself is tested (indirect_array_walk_over_the_bounds_is_reported)

Edited tree, elements reachable only from the /ParentTree or /IDTree (not from the root /K) are not read by the new clause (the purge neutralizes the ones the parent tree maps to a flattened page); malformed input, not probed

An element whose own /Pg names a kept page is accepted even if the flattened page's parent-tree entry also names it (contradictory input). By reading, not probed: the saved flattened page does not keep /StructParents, so check_document has no key to look up. The same holds for a child below an unread array whose ancestor has a kept /Pg while the child's MCIDs sit on the flattened page

An element dictionary is a dictionary with /S (the criterion neutralize_structure uses); a dictionary with /Type /StructElem and no /S is not walked as an element, by the purge or by the check (not probed)
A trailer /Root reached through a chain of references makes edited_structure_root None (dict_of(catalog) is None) so the tree is walked by the direct-root rule; covered by construction, no test
A /StructTreeRoot that is a reference to a non-dictionary has no tree to walk (0)
The same element reachable both through a direct and through an unread edge is judged on the first visit (a reference is walked once); two parents for one element is malformed input
